_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Qatar covering Dilmun trade links, Sasanian forts, early Islamic period, pearl diving economy, Al Thani family rise (1825), Ottoman suzerainty, British protectorate 1916, oil discovery 1940 (Dukhan field), independence 1971, Hamad's 1995 coup, Al Jazeera 1996, North Field (world's largest gas field), 2022 FIFA World Cup, and regional diplomatic crises.

religion.note: Sunni Wahhabi official; state religion; shari'a influences law; religious freedom for non-Muslims limited but relatively tolerant by Gulf standards; expatriate workforce diverse (Hindu, Christian)

ethnic_groups.name: Qatari Arab
ethnic_groups.notes: Citizens are minority; Al Thani ruling family; tribal structure; Bedouin heritage; oil/gas wealth per capita highest globally; privileged welfare state

ethnic_groups.name: Other Arab (Egyptian, Jordanian, Palestinian, Lebanese, Syrian)
ethnic_groups.notes: Professionals, teachers, service workers; Palestinians given preference historically

ethnic_groups.name: South Asian (Indian, Nepali, Bangladeshi, Pakistani, Sri Lankan)
ethnic_groups.notes: Largest group; construction workers (kafala system); service sector; Indians ~700,000 (largest single nationality); exploitative labor conditions for some

ethnic_groups.name: Other (Iranian, European, African)
ethnic_groups.notes: Western professionals (oil/gas, education); Iranian merchants; African workers

country_profile.notes_unique: World's highest GDP per capita by some measures; North Field (world's largest single gas reservoir, shared with Iran as South Pars); Al Jazeera (Arabic news network, 1996, controversial); 2022 FIFA World Cup (first Middle East host, winter timing, kafala system abuses exposed); 2017-2021 blockade by Saudi/UAE/Bahrain/Egypt; tiny peninsula;EducationCity; Museum of Islamic Art (I.M. Pei); kafala sponsorship system reformed 2020

current_leader.name: Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani
current_leader.title: Emir
current_leader.notes: Al Thani dynasty; succeeded father Hamad (who abdicated); youngest reigning monarch in region; survived 2017-2021 blockade; 2022 World Cup; assertive foreign policy; Al Jazeera patron; closer to Turkey/Iran than neighbors

former_emirs.name: Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani
former_emirs.notes: Deposed father Khalifa in bloodless coup (1995); transformed Qatar into global player; founded Al Jazeera 1996; education/healthcare investments; North Field gas development; women's rights advances; abdicated in favor of son Tamim (rare Gulf abdication)

former_emirs.name: Khalifa bin Hamad Al Thani
former_emirs.notes: Deposed cousin Ahmad (1972); oil boom; infrastructure; deposed by son Hamad while in Switzerland

former_emirs.name: Ahmad bin Ali Al Thani
former_emirs.notes: Oil wealth began; ousted by cousin Khalifa while abroad

former_emirs.name: Ali bin Abdullah Al Thani
former_emirs.notes: Abdicated in favor of son Ahmad; early oil era

910.name: Ancient Qatar and Early Settlements
910.description: The prehistoric and ancient settlements of the Qatar peninsula, connections to the Dilmun and Ubaid cultures, Ptolemy's mention of 'Catara,' and the Sassanid period.

sub_clusters.name: Prehistoric and Dilmun Connections
sub_clusters.description: Stone Age flint tools found on the Qatar peninsula, the Ubaid-period pottery indicating Mesopotamian connections, links to the Dilmun trading network, and Ptolemy's reference to 'Catara.'
key_events: Ptolemy's Geography includes 'Catara' — earliest known written reference to Qatar (2nd century AD)

sub_clusters.name: Sassanid and Late Antique Qatar
sub_clusters.description: The Qatar peninsula under Seleucid, Parthian, and Sassanid influence, purple dye production from murex shells, early Nestorian Christian communities, and pre-Islamic Arab tribes.

920.name: Early Islamic Qatar and Medieval Trade
920.description: Qatar's early conversion to Islam, its role in the Ridda Wars, the pearl diving economy under Abbasid and Carmathian rule, and the medieval Gulf trade networks.

sub_clusters.name: Conversion and Ridda Wars
sub_clusters.description: The acceptance of Islam by the tribes of Qatar, their participation in the Ridda Wars after the Prophet's death, and the integration into the Rashidun and Umayyad caliphates.
key_events: Al-Mundhir ibn Sawa, ruler of the region including Qatar, accepts Islam (628 AD)

sub_clusters.name: Carmathian and Medieval Pearl Economy
sub_clusters.description: The Carmathian revolt's impact on eastern Arabia, the development of Qatar's pearl diving industry, the Uyunid and Jabrid dynasties, and the region's role in Indian Ocean trade.

930.name: Portuguese, Ottoman, and Early Modern Qatar
930.description: European and Ottoman competition in the Gulf, the devastating Portuguese raids, Ottoman nominal suzerainty, and the gradual emergence of settled communities on the peninsula.

sub_clusters.name: Portuguese and Ottoman Period
sub_clusters.description: Portuguese naval raids on Qatari coastal settlements, the Ottoman assertion of control over eastern Arabia, and the sparse population eking out a living from pearling and fishing.

sub_clusters.name: Al-Khalifa Settlement and Zubarah
sub_clusters.description: The migration of the Bani Utbah including the Al-Khalifa family to Zubarah on Qatar's northwest coast, the town's growth into a major pearl-trading center, and the founding of the Zubarah fort.
key_events: Zubarah develops as a major pearl-trading and mercantile center (mid-18th century)

930.name: Al-Thani Dynasty Foundation
930.description: The Al-Khalifa departure for Bahrain, the rise of the Al-Thani family, the Ottoman garrison period, and the establishment of British treaty relations.

sub_clusters.name: Al-Khalifa Departure and Al-Thani Rise
sub_clusters.description: The Al-Khalifa family's conquest of Bahrain and departure from Qatar, the power vacuum, the emergence of Muhammad bin Thani as the leading sheikh, and the 1868 British treaty recognizing Qatari autonomy.
key_events: Treaty with Lewis Pelly — Britain recognizes Qatar as a separate entity from Bahrain (1868)

sub_clusters.name: Ottoman Garrison and Jassim bin Muhammad Al-Thani
sub_clusters.description: The Ottoman garrison at Doha, Sheikh Jassim's complex relationship with the Ottomans including armed resistance, the Battle of Al Wajbah, and the emergence of Qatar's founder figure.
key_events: Battle of Al Wajbah — Jassim's forces defeat the Ottoman garrison, Qatar's founding battle (March 1893)
Jassim bin Muhammad Al-Thani dies, revered as the founder of the State of Qatar (1913)

940.name: British Protectorate and Oil Era
940.description: Qatar under British protection, the decline of the pearl industry, the discovery of oil at Dukhan, and the journey to independence.

sub_clusters.name: Treaty Era and Pearl Decline
sub_clusters.description: The 1916 Anglo-Qatari Treaty establishing the protectorate, the collapse of the pearl industry due to Japanese cultured pearls, extreme poverty, and the first oil concessions.
key_events: Oil discovered at Dukhan field on the west coast (1939)
First export of oil from Qatar (1949)

sub_clusters.name: Oil Wealth and Independence
sub_clusters.description: The rapid transformation from poverty to wealth, Sheikh Khalifa's modernization, the failed federation attempt with the Trucial States, and Qatar's declaration of independence.

950.name: Modern Qatar and LNG Revolution
950.description: Post-independence state-building, the discovery of the massive North Field gas reservoir, the 1995 palace coup, and Qatar's emergence as the world's leading LNG exporter.

sub_clusters.name: Post-Independence and North Field Discovery
sub_clusters.description: Sheikh Khalifa bin Hamad's nation-building, the nationalization of oil, the 1971 border dispute with Bahrain, and the transformative discovery of the North Field — the world's largest natural gas reservoir.
key_events: North Field discovered — the world's single largest non-associated natural gas reservoir (1971)

sub_clusters.name: 1995 Coup and Al Jazeera
sub_clusters.description: Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa's bloodless palace coup deposing his father, the founding of Al Jazeera satellite news network, massive LNG investments, and Qatar's repositioning as a regional power.
key_events: Sheikh Hamad deposes his father in a bloodless palace coup (June 27, 1995)
Al Jazeera satellite news channel launches from Doha (November 1, 1996)

950.name: Qatar as Global Actor
950.description: Qatar's transformation into a disproportionately influential global actor through Al Jazeera, sovereign wealth, sports diplomacy, and mediation — culminating in the 2017 Gulf blockade.

sub_clusters.name: Mediation and Soft Power
sub_clusters.description: Qatar's mediation in Lebanon, Darfur, and other conflicts, the Education City and cultural investments, the Al Udeid Air Base hosting US CENTCOM, and the 2022 World Cup bid.
key_events: Qatar wins the bid to host the 2022 FIFA World Cup (December 2010)
Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad becomes Emir after his father's abdication (June 2013)

sub_clusters.name: Gulf Blockade
sub_clusters.description: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Bahrain, and Egypt's diplomatic and economic blockade of Qatar, the accusations of terrorism financing, Qatar's self-sufficiency drive, and the Al-Ula resolution.
key_events: Saudi-led bloc imposes land, sea, and air blockade on Qatar (June 5, 2017)
Al-Ula Declaration ends the Gulf blockade (January 5, 2021)

960.name: World Cup Era and National Vision 2030
960.description: Qatar's hosting of the 2022 FIFA World Cup, the Qatar National Vision 2030 diversification strategy, labor reforms, and the country's positioning as a knowledge and energy hub.

sub_clusters.name: 2022 FIFA World Cup
sub_clusters.description: The massive infrastructure buildout for the World Cup, the construction of stadiums and metro systems, international scrutiny of labor conditions, reforms to the kafala system, and the tournament itself.
key_events: Doha Metro opens as part of World Cup infrastructure (2019)
Qatar hosts the FIFA World Cup — the first in the Middle East (November–December 2022)

sub_clusters.name: Post-World Cup and Diversification
sub_clusters.description: Qatar's post-tournament legacy planning, the North Field expansion making Qatar the world's largest LNG exporter, the Qatar Investment Authority's global portfolio, and Vision 2030 progress.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
